bullets.title: Foundations of Pharmacology and Medication Safety
bullets.text: Pharmacology is the study of medicines and their effects on the body. Nurses do not need to memorise every medicine, but they must understand the principles that explain why a medicine is given, how it works, what effects are expected and what risks require monitoring. bullets.title: Calculating, Preparing and Administering Medicines Safely
bullets.text: Medication administration combines calculation, practical skill and professional judgement. A correct order can still cause harm if the dose is calculated incorrectly, the wrong route is used or the medicine is given without identifying the patient. Reliable safety checks should be followed even during busy periods.

bullets.title: Preventing Errors and Recognising Adverse Reactions
bullets.text: Medication safety continues after a medicine is given. Nurses must observe for benefit, side effects, allergy, interaction and deterioration. Early recognition and prompt action can prevent a mild reaction from becoming a serious emergency.

bullets.title: Accountability, Documentation and Patient Education
bullets.text: Safe medication practice is both a clinical and professional responsibility. Nurses must practise within their authority, document accurately and ensure that patients understand how to use medicines safely. Medication education is not an optional extra; it is part of effective treatment.
